title: 2022 HMMT November General Problem 5
statement: An apartment building consists of 20 rooms numbered \(1,2, \ldots, 20\) arranged clockwise in a circle. To move from one room to another, one can either walk to the next room clockwise (i.e. from room \(i\) to room \((i+1)(\bmod 20))\) or walk across the center to the opposite room (i.e. from room \(i\) to room \((i+10)(\bmod 20))\). Find the number of ways to move from room 10 to room 20 without visiting the same room twice.

solutions.text:
One way is to walk directly from room 10 to 20 . Else, divide the rooms into 10 pairs \(A_{0}=(10,20), A_{1}=(1,11), A_{2}=(2,12), \ldots, A_{9}=(9,19)\). Notice that

- each move is either between rooms in \(A_{i}\) and \(A_{(i+1)(\bmod 10)}\) for some \(i \in\{0,1, \ldots, 9\}\), or between rooms in the same pair, meaning that our path must pass through \(A_{0}, A_{1}, \ldots, A_{9}\) in that order before coming back to room 20 in \(A_{0}\),
- in each of the pairs \(A_{1}, A_{2}, \ldots, A_{8}\), we can choose to walk between rooms in that pair 0 or 1 times, and
- we have to walk between rooms 9 and 19 if and only if we first reach \(A_{9}\) at room 9 (so the choice of walking between \(A_{9}\) is completely determined by previous choices).

Thus, the number of ways to walk from room 10 to 20 is \(1+2^{8}=257\).
